title: The Room in Lakshmipuram: the Sanskrit Professor, the Sequence, and the Manuscript Nobody Saw
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Priest's Son in the Hassan Hills

stops.name: Kowshika, birth on the full moon
stops.date_confidence: attested as to date; the coordinate is Hassan town, the district seat, because no source consulted gives one for the village
stops.campa: On the full-moon day of Guru Purnima a son is born to a priest and astrologer in the village of Kowshika, in the hill country near Hassan, in the Kingdom of Mysore. The household keeps the rites of a rural agrahara: ritual fire, cattle, Sanskrit chanted before light. The kingdom around it is ruled from a palace a long day's travel east that the boy will not see for fifteen years. No source reached here gives a coordinate for the hamlet itself; the pin sits on the district town, and the village lies somewhere in its hills.
suggested_refs: Kowshika village, Hassan district, Karnataka, unmapped in reachable gazetteers

stops.name: Bettadapura, the second birthplace
stops.date_confidence: contradiction: a competing tradition places the birth here rather than at Kowshika, and nothing reached this session adjudicates between them
stops.campa: A second tradition puts the birth not in the Hassan hills but at Bettadapura, in Periyapatna taluk of Mysore district, eighty-two kilometers from the city. The two claims do not reconcile in any source reached here, and neither carries a citation the other lacks. A founder's birthplace is the one fact a lineage wants fixed, and this one is not fixed. Both are small villages in Kannada country. Either one puts the same rites and the same Sanskrit around the infant on the same full-moon day.
suggested_refs: Bettadapura, Periyapatna taluk, Mysuru district, 12 degrees 27 minutes 14 seconds N, 76 degrees 06 minutes 58 seconds E

stops.name: Kowshika, the school and the boy of five
stops.date_confidence: tradition only; the institute's own telling, undated in any contemporary record, and irreconcilable with the Hassan account below
stops.campa: The institute's own telling has a demonstration by Tirumalai Krishnamacharya reaching the village school when the boy is five, years before the meeting every biography repeats. His father is teaching him Sanskrit and the household ritual in the same years, by lineage account rather than by record. Neither story is footnoted to anything contemporary; both descend from oral retelling decades after the fact, by the man himself and by those who trained under him. The lineage keeps both accounts and dates neither of them.
suggested_refs: The five-years-old version of the first encounter, circulated in secondary Ashtanga histories
sources: Institute oral tradition as relayed in secondary Ashtanga histories
Wikipedia, 'K. Pattabhi Jois' (which gives the age-twelve version instead)

stops.name: Hassan, the demonstration at Jubilee Hall
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year; no source gives the month or the day
stops.campa: At twelve he is taken to Jubilee Hall in Hassan, a colonial public building used for lectures and civic gatherings, where Krishnamacharya demonstrates asana before the town. He presents himself the next day and is accepted. For the next two years he practices under Krishnamacharya in and around his own village. Every biography of both men repeats this hour in a district-town hall, and the hall itself draws no attention beside what is said to have happened inside it.
suggested_refs: Jubilee Hall, Hassan, venue of the 1927 lecture-demonstration

stops.name: The Hassan road, two rupees and no blessing
stops.date_confidence: the departure year is attested; the route is not, and this pin is a midpoint on the Hassan to Mysore line rather than a place any source puts him
stops.campa: At fourteen, or fifteen after his July birthday, he leaves the village for Mysore with two rupees and without his family's blessing, to study Sanskrit. The distance is about a hundred and twenty kilometers of hill and plain. No itinerary survives and no waystation is named; the story exists as a departure and an arrival with the road between them unrecorded. Wikipedia's summary says fifteen, other accounts say thirteen or fourteen, and the arithmetic of a July birthday says both can be defended. He will not live anywhere else again.
suggested_refs: The Hassan to Mysore road, about 120 km, unrecorded as an itinerary
sources: Traditional accounts repeated across Ashtanga biographies

stops.name: Maharaja's Sanskrit College, the student arrives
stops.date_confidence: the year and the Sanskrit-study motive are attested; the month is placed for ordering and is not sourced
stops.campa: He enrolls at the Maharaja's Sanskrit College in Mysore, living on close to nothing while he studies grammar and scripture. Mysore in these years is a small capital arranged entirely around its palace and the enthusiasms of its ruler, and yoga is among them. Krishnamacharya is already in the same city under the patronage of Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, but the two do not find each other again for two more years. The student who walked in with two rupees will keep this city as his only address for seventy-nine years.
suggested_refs: The Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore, where he studied and later taught for thirty-six years

stops.name: Mysore Palace, the teacher found again
stops.date_confidence: the 1932 reunion is attested; whether Jois attended any session inside the palace before the Jaganmohan yogashala opened is not established anywhere reached here
stops.campa: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV has kept Krishnamacharya since 1926, installed at Amba Vilas as something between court physician and instructor of the discipline. In 1932 Jois is reunited with him and resumes formal study. This is the same palace where, forty years earlier, Chamarajendra Wodeyar received Swami Vivekananda and offered to pay his passage to America; the Maharaja who now funds yoga in these rooms is that Maharaja's son. One dynasty pays for two exports of Indian practice to the West, a generation apart.
suggested_refs: Amba Vilas, the Mysore Palace, patron seat of Krishnamacharya from 1926

stops.name: Mysore, the marriage to Savitramma
stops.date_confidence: attested as to month and year; other secondary accounts give other years without citing anything
stops.campa: In June 1933 he marries Savitramma, whom the household will call Amma. They will have three children: Saraswathi, Manju, and Ramesh. She runs the house that becomes, fifteen years later, the address of a yoga institute, and later still an address foreigners write down before booking a flight to India. He is seventeen and a Sanskrit student with no income. What he has to bring to the marriage is a teacher and a practice done before dawn. Nothing in the arrangement suggests that the house is the asset.
suggested_refs: Savitramma 'Amma' Jois, who kept the household that became the institute

stops.name: Jaganmohan Palace, the yogashala opens
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: On the eleventh of August 1933 the Maharaja grants Krishnamacharya a wing of the Jaganmohan Palace for a yogashala, an institution separate from the Sanskrit College. Jois trains here through the thirties and forties and into the early fifties: the Yoga Sutras, the Hatha Yoga Pradipika, and the sequence of postures linked to breath that he will later fix as Ashtanga. The palace stands today in central Mysore as a public art gallery. The room where the method took its shape draws fewer visitors than the paintings.
stops.quote: If your breath strength is possibly ten-second inhalations and exhalations, you do ten; fifteen seconds possible, you do fifteen.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Pattabhi Jois, 'On Vinyasa', Ashtanga Yoga Shala NYC, quoted in Wikipedia, 'Ashtanga vinyasa yoga'; the shala page itself now returns 404
suggested_refs: The Jaganmohan Palace yogashala wing, opened 11 August 1933

stops.name: Jaganmohan Palace, the text nobody else has seen
stops.date_confidence: undated: the teaching is attested, the manuscript is not, and the date here marks the period of instruction rather than an event
stops.campa: Krishnamacharya teaches the sequences as the contents of a manuscript, the Yoga Korunta, attributed to a sage called Vamana Rishi. Jois will repeat the attribution for the rest of his life. No outside scholar ever sees it, and the accounts of its provenance do not agree: found in the National Archives of India, written in Nepali, later eaten by ants, in one telling; copied from a palm leaf in Calcutta in another. Krishnamacharya cites it nowhere in his own Yoga Makaranda of 1934. The sequence is real and its charter is missing.
suggested_refs: The Yoga Korunta, attributed to Vamana Rishi, unseen by any scholar outside the lineage

segments.name: The College, the Palace, and the Empty Throne

stops.name: Sanskrit College, the yoga post
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year
stops.campa: From 1937 he teaches yoga at the Sanskrit College where he had been the penniless student, the same institution that first brought Krishnamacharya under royal pay. He will hold the post thirty-six years. He teaches scripture and grammar by day; in the evening a slowly growing number of students sit on the floor of his own front room. The two roles are not yet separable in Mysore's institutional life, and nobody in the city treats the second as a career. They separate only when students start arriving from outside India and paying to be taught.
suggested_refs: His teaching appointment at the Sanskrit College, Mysore, 1937 to 1973

stops.name: Bangalore, the death of the Maharaja
stops.date_confidence: attested as to date; the location is given as Bangalore in general histories
stops.campa: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV dies on the third of August 1940. His successor has little interest in yoga, and the princely state itself has eight years left before it is folded into a republic. The patronage that built the yogashala begins draining from the day of the funeral. Jois by now teaches on a state college salary and does not depend on the palace. The lineage survives him. The arrangement whereby a king personally paid for a yoga hall inside his own palace does not.
suggested_refs: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV, patron of the Jaganmohan yogashala, died 3 August 1940
sources: General historical record of Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV

stops.name: Lakshmipuram, the institute in the front room
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year; the coordinate follows the geography pass, against an afterlife-pass figure some 700 m north
stops.campa: In 1948 he founds the Ashtanga Yoga Research Institute at his own house in Lakshmipuram, a residential quarter of Mysore. There is no patron. The Maharaja is eight years dead, India is one year independent, and he builds an institution that answers to nobody rather than wait for a court that no longer wants one. The word research is his. For the next fifty-four years this house is the address the whole discipline answers to, and students from California, Italy, and Japan will be given the same directions to the same gate.
stops.quote: You completely exhale, apply mula bandha and after inhaling you apply uddiyana bandha. Both bandhas are very important... After bandha practice, take [your attention] to the location where they are applied and maintain that attention at all times, while walking, talking, sleeping and when walk is finished. Always you control mula bandha.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Pattabhi Jois, 'On Pranayama, Bandha and Drishti', Ashtanga Yoga Shala NYC, archived copy, transcribed in Wikipedia, 'Ashtanga vinyasa yoga'; the archive host was not reachable from this session
suggested_refs: The Lakshmipuram house, seat of the Ashtanga Yoga Research Institute from 1948 to 2002

stops.name: Jaganmohan Palace, the yogashala closed
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year
stops.campa: In 1950 the yogashala in the palace wing is closed by order of the first Chief Minister of the new state. The royal money is gone and the republic has other priorities than a king's yoga hall. Krishnamacharya's formal institution ends, and what continues does so in private houses, one teacher to one student, unfunded and unregistered. Jois teaches at the college and receives students at Lakshmipuram, and the practice outlasts the closing of the only building that ever housed it officially.
suggested_refs: The closure of the Jaganmohan yogashala by order of the Chief Minister, 1950

stops.name: Madras, the teacher goes to the coast
stops.date_confidence: contradiction: Wikipedia's Krishnamacharya article gives 1952, the Jois article implies 1953; neither is preferred here
stops.campa: Krishnamacharya is invited to Madras as a lecturer at Vivekananda College and leaves Mysore for good. Jois stays. The two men, joined since the Hassan demonstration of 1927, never again teach at one address: Krishnamacharya has thirty-seven years left, Jois fifty-seven. Mysore is now his alone to define, and he defines it as an institute in his own front room, with no signboard, no staff, and no students from further away than the next district. Sources disagree on whether the move was 1952 or 1953, and on nothing else about it.
suggested_refs: Vivekananda College, Madras, Krishnamacharya's post from the early 1950s

stops.name: Adyar, the corridor that will carry them
stops.date_confidence: context pin, not travel: no source places Pattabhi Jois at Adyar or anywhere in Madras, and the date marks Krishnamacharya's presence in the city rather than his student's
stops.campa: A few kilometers down the coast from Krishnamacharya's new employer stands the Theosophical Society compound at Adyar, moved here from Bombay in 1882 by Helena Blavatsky, run for decades by Annie Besant, and used as a lodging by Hermann Keyserling in 1911 on his way inland. Nothing reached here puts Jois on this ground. The pin is the corridor, not the man: every Western student who reaches Mysore for the next fifty years comes up this same coast, along rails and ports laid for other traffic entirely.
suggested_refs: The Theosophical Society headquarters at Adyar, shared pin with blavatsky, annie_besant, and keyserling

stops.name: Sanskrit College, made vidwan
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year
stops.campa: In 1956 the college makes him vidwan, senior professor, a title for mastery of Sanskrit learning and not for anything done on a mat. He is forty-one and has taught in the building for nineteen years. The honour lands in a life that has so far produced no book, no foreign student, and no institution larger than a room behind a house in Lakshmipuram. Nobody in Mysore, himself included, has any reason to expect a second half to this career, still less one conducted in California.
suggested_refs: The title of vidwan conferred at the Sanskrit College, Mysore, 1956

stops.name: Mysore, the writing of Yoga Mala
stops.date_confidence: contradiction: Wikipedia's article on Jois dates the Kannada original to 1958, its article on Ashtanga vinyasa yoga to 1962, and nothing reached here reconciles them
stops.campa: He writes Yoga Mala in Kannada, a manual of the primary sequence: the postures in their order, the breath count, the bandhas, the drishti, argued by a Sanskritist rather than demonstrated by a gymnast. The publication year is not settled between the sources. It will wait four decades for an English translation, and by then the readers waiting for it will be on other continents and will have learned the sequence from students of students, out of order, without the book.
stops.quote: It is sufficient, however, to breathe in and out five to eight times in each posture.
stops.quote_source: K. Pattabhi Jois, Yoga Mala, trans. Eddie Stern (North Point Press, 2002), p. 108, as cited in Wikipedia, 'Ashtanga vinyasa yoga'
suggested_refs: Yoga Mala, Kannada first edition, dated 1958 or 1962 depending on the source

segments.name: The First Foreigners at the Gate

stops.name: Lakshmipuram, the hall behind the house
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year for both the extension and Van Lysebeth's two months; which of his books carries the account is unverified
stops.campa: In 1964 he builds a proper hall behind the Lakshmipuram house, the front room having stopped fitting the students. The same year Andre Van Lysebeth, a Belgian pranayama teacher and author, studies with him for two months and afterwards puts his name in print for a European readership. It is among the first appearances of the name Pattabhi Jois in a Western language. The door that opens for one Belgian visitor in 1964 does not close again for the rest of the century.
suggested_refs: Andre Van Lysebeth's two months of study at Lakshmipuram, 1964

stops.name: Lakshmipuram, the first American at the gate
stops.date_confidence: year uncertain, 1971 or 1972; his precedence as the first Western student is the attested part
stops.campa: Norman Allen, generally counted the first Western student, reaches Mysore around 1971 after seeing Manju Jois give a demonstration. He finds a residential street, a family house, and a teacher who has been doing this for forty-four years without anyone from outside the district noticing. The year is not fixed in the sources reached here. He arrives alone, one American on a Lakshmipuram street asking a Sanskrit professor to let him in, and nobody has yet thought to call this a movement.
suggested_refs: Norman Allen, generally described as Jois's first Western student
sources: Secondary Ashtanga histories; Wikipedia, 'K. Pattabhi Jois'

stops.name: Lakshmipuram, Williams and Gilgoff
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year
stops.campa: David Williams and Nancy Gilgoff arrive in 1973 and stay to learn the full method. Two years later the pair of them will organize and pay for the first visit of Jois and his son Manju to California. Historians of the practice date the export of Ashtanga to this arrival. There is no sign on the house and the institute consists of one man; two young Americans sit on his floor copying a sequence into notebooks, and the sequence in those notebooks reaches four continents.
suggested_refs: David Williams and Nancy Gilgoff, sponsors of the 1975 Encinitas visit

stops.name: Sanskrit College, the professorship ends
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year; the month is placed for ordering and is not sourced
stops.campa: The same year, after thirty-six of them, his post at the college ends and he gives the whole of his time to the institute. The salary that made him independent of patrons is gone; the foreign students who will replace it number two. He is fifty-eight. From here his living comes from people who cross an ocean to reach a house in Lakshmipuram, which changes what the practice is for and whose it is, though nobody in the room says so at the time. He has thirty-six years of teaching behind him and thirty-six ahead of him, and almost everyone in the second set arrives from abroad.
suggested_refs: The end of the Sanskrit College appointment, 1973

stops.name: Mysore, the first passage out of India
stops.date_confidence: the fact and the year are attested; the country, city, month and conference name are a gap, the source naming only the continent
stops.campa: In 1974, at fifty-nine, he leaves the subcontinent for the first time, flying to South America to lecture in Sanskrit at an international yoga conference. The source consulted names the continent and nothing else: no country, no city, no title, no date inside the year. He speaks in a language most of the hall cannot follow, about a practice most of the hall has never seen, and comes home to the same house and the same students. The following year he crosses an ocean again, brought over and paid for by two of his own students.
suggested_refs: The 1974 South American yoga conference, unidentified as to country and city

stops.name: Encinitas, four months in California
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year and duration; the month is not given
stops.campa: Brought over by Williams and Gilgoff, Jois and his son Manju spend four months in Encinitas, a beach town north of San Diego, teaching the sequence he has taught in one Mysore room since 1948. It is the first sustained teaching he does on foreign soil, and American Ashtanga dates itself from these four months; studios still trace their descent through this one visit. He is sixty years old and has been practicing for forty-eight of them, all but four in the same two neighbourhoods of one city.
stops.quote: gradually, gradually, in twenty years, it will be fully spreading
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Jois on Ashtanga's prospects in America, cited to Eddie Stern (2002) in Wikipedia, 'K. Pattabhi Jois'; Stern's original not read this session
suggested_refs: The 1975 Encinitas visit, origin point of American Ashtanga

stops.name: Government College of Indian Medicine, the honorary chair
stops.date_confidence: attested as a 1976 to 1978 appointment; one source gives the range as 1976/1978 without further detail
stops.campa: From 1976 to 1978 the Indian state gives him an honorary professorship of yoga at the Government College of Indian Medicine in Mysore. Recognition arrives from his own country in the exact years the traffic from other countries begins. The chair is modest beside what is happening in his front hall, where paying foreigners are starting to outnumber the Sanskrit colleagues who were, for four decades, the only public identity he had. He keeps both. The Sanskrit is not decoration to him.
suggested_refs: Honorary Professor of Yoga, Government College of Indian Medicine, Mysore, 1976 to 1978

stops.name: Mysore, the grandson at nineteen
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year
stops.campa: Sharath, son of his daughter Saraswathi, begins formal study of the system at nineteen and does not stop. He will travel with his grandfather through the nineties, take the teaching floor in 2007, and hold the lineage's central authority for seventeen years. In 1990 he is simply another body on the floor of a room in his own family's house, learning a sequence from a man who is both his teacher and his grandfather. The succession is settled a long time before anyone calls it one.
stops.quote: Yoga practice and the correct breathing system. Practice, practice, practice. That's it. Practice so the nervous system is perfect and the blood circulation is good, which is very important.
stops.quote_source: Sandra Anderson, 'Practice Makes Perfect: An Interview with Sri K. Pattabhi Jois', Yoga International, Jan/Feb 1994, reproduced at ashtangidiary.blogspot.com and fetched directly
suggested_refs: R. Sharath Jois, who began formal study under his grandfather in 1990

stops.name: San Francisco, the student who loosened it
stops.date_confidence: the 1991 founding of It's Yoga and the 1982 workshop are attested; the workshop's city is not named in any source reached here
stops.campa: Larry Schultz meets Jois in 1982 at a United States workshop organized by Stan Hafner, in a city no source reached here names. He studies with him seven years, in India and America, returns to San Francisco in 1989, and in 1991 opens It's Yoga, where the sequence is taught out of order and to the student's convenience. A photograph survives of the two men together, captioned only mid 1980s, with no place given. Jois's own objection to what America is doing with the sequence reaches print four years later.
suggested_refs: It's Yoga, San Francisco, founded by Larry Schultz in 1991

stops.name: Mysore, the letter to Yoga Journal
stops.date_confidence: attested as to month and year; the letter itself was read in reproduction
stops.campa: In November 1995 he writes to Yoga Journal about the American product being sold as Power Yoga, taken from his sequence and detached from everything that surrounded it. He cites Yoga Sutra II.28 on the practice that burns off impurity, and closes on the image of a jewel of liberation dropped in mud. He is eighty, writing from Mysore to a magazine in California about the misuse of a method he learned in a palace wing from a man who said he had it out of a manuscript nobody has ever seen.
stops.quote: Power is the property of God. It is not something to be collected for one's ego.
stops.quote_source: Letter from Sri K. Pattabhi Jois to Yoga Journal, November 1995, reproduced on aylibrary.blogspot.com and fetched directly
suggested_refs: The November 1995 letter to Yoga Journal against 'Power Yoga'
sources: aylibrary.blogspot.com, 'A letter from Sri K. Pattabhi Jois to Yoga Journal' (2012)

stops.name: Puck Building, Manhattan, a workshop in the nineties
stops.date_confidence: the venue is attested by Anneke Lucas's 2016 account, which gives no year; 1996 is a placeholder inside the attested workshop period and is not a sourced date
stops.campa: He teaches workshops in New York through the nineties and the two thousands, one of them at the Puck Building on Lafayette Street. Anneke Lucas, in an account published on YogaCityNYC in 2016, says he assaulted her during an adjustment at a Jois workshop in this building. Hers is the earliest of the published testimonies and comes two years before the wave that follows. The year of the workshop is not given. The room is full, the mats are in rows, and the teacher walks between them putting his hands on people.
suggested_refs: The Puck Building, 295 Lafayette Street, Manhattan, venue of a Jois workshop of unstated year
sources: Anneke Lucas, YogaCityNYC.com (2016), not fetched this session, reported through the verified research pool

stops.name: Broome Street, the book in English
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year; the publisher is corrected against a common misattribution to North Point Press, which issued its own edition in 2002
stops.campa: Yoga Mala appears in English in 1999, translated by Eddie Stern and published by his own Patanjali Yoga Shala on Broome Street rather than by any trade house. North Point Press issues its edition in 2002 and reprints in 2010 and 2017. Four decades after the Kannada original, the manual reaches the readers who had been practicing out of it at second and third hand. A Spanish edition follows, and a Chinese one in Taiwan in 2015, in a language the author could not read.
stops.quote: Yoga is ninety-nine percent practice and one percent theory.
stops.quote_source: An oral maxim of Jois recorded by Eddie Stern in Yoga Mala (North Point Press, 2002); in his own 1994 Yoga International interview Jois gave the variant 'Yoga is 95 percent practical. Only 5 percent is theory.'
suggested_refs: Yoga Mala, first English edition, Patanjali Yoga Shala / Ashtanga Yoga New York, 1999
sources: Open Library records for Yoga Mala editions

stops.name: Gokulam, the purpose-built school
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year; the coordinate follows the afterlife pass against a geography-pass figure some 1.3 km east
stops.campa: In 2002 he opens a larger building in Gokulam, a growing quarter north of the old city, because Lakshmipuram cannot hold the numbers. What was a room behind a family house becomes an institute with a registration desk and a waiting list. Students come to Mysore for this and for nothing else, staying months, renting flats in the streets around it. The name of the city has become, in yoga rooms on four continents, the name of a style: people say they are doing Mysore who will never go there.
suggested_refs: The Gokulam school building, opened 2002

stops.name: Gokulam, the adjustments
stops.date_confidence: the practice is attested across the 1990s and 2000s; the single year here is a marker for a continuous period, not an event
stops.campa: He teaches by hand, pressing students further into postures than they will press themselves, and has taught this way since the yogashala. The Economist's obituary will record students limping with injured knees and backs from his adjustments. Inside the room this is understood as the method itself: the teacher moves the body where the body declines to go. The women who will later describe what else happened during those adjustments are, in these years, still practicing in these rows and saying nothing.
stops.quote: a good number of Mr Jois's students seemed constantly to be limping around with injured knees or backs because they had received his 'adjustments'
stops.quote_source: Obituary of K. Pattabhi Jois, The Economist, 4 June 2009, as quoted in Wikipedia, 'K. Pattabhi Jois'; the obituary itself was not fetched this session
suggested_refs: The Economist obituary of 4 June 2009 on his adjustment style
sources: Wikipedia, 'K. Pattabhi Jois', citing The Economist

stops.name: Gokulam, the grandson takes the floor
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year
stops.campa: His health fails to the point where he can no longer teach, and Sharath becomes director of the institute. Jois is ninety-two and has taught without a break since 1937. The handover is domestic rather than ceremonial: the grandson has been in the room since 1990 and the room continues with one teacher fewer in it. Foreign students who booked a season with the founder arrive to find him off the floor, watching, and are taught the same sequence by a man of thirty-five.
suggested_refs: R. Sharath Jois's assumption of the directorship, 2007

stops.name: Lakshmipuram, the death
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; cause of death is not given in any source reached here
stops.campa: Pattabhi Jois dies on the eighteenth of May 2009 in Mysore, at ninety-three, seventy-nine years after walking into the city with two rupees. He never moved to another. The obituaries name him a guru, a Sanskrit professor, and the man who put a Mysore sequence into several hundred thousand Western bodies. The accusations that will reorganize his reputation are, on the day of the funeral, still unpublished; the first of them appears seven years later.
stops.quote: He was not a monk or a renunciate; he was fearless about combining the path of yogi with the path of participant.
stops.quote_source: David Life, co-founder of Jivamukti Yoga, quoted in Amanda Fortini, 'Ommm Sweaty', New York Magazine, 15-22 June 2009; often misattributed to the New York Times
suggested_refs: Amanda Fortini, 'Ommm Sweaty', New York Magazine, June 2009

stops.name: Mysore, the cremation unrecorded
stops.date_confidence: inferred: the death in Mysore is attested, the cremation is not documented in anything reached here as to date, site, or rite
stops.campa: He is cremated in Mysore. No source reached here names the ground, the hour, or who lit the fire, and none records a samadhi shrine, a tomb, a statue, a museum, or a stamp; the absence is a gap in the searching, not proof that nothing was raised. The city that takes the ashes is the city he walked into at fourteen with two rupees and no plan beyond finding a man he had watched give one demonstration in a district-town hall. Seventy-nine years lie between the arrival and the fire, and almost all of them are spent on two streets of this city.
suggested_refs: No cremation site, tomb, shrine, statue, or monument located in any source reached
sources: Gap: exhausted search and fetch attempts

stops.name: Gokulam, the institute takes his name
stops.date_confidence: the renaming is attested to 2009, the year of his death; the month is placed for ordering
stops.campa: In the year of his death the Ashtanga Yoga Research Institute becomes the K. Pattabhi Jois Ashtanga Yoga Institute. The word research is retired and the name of a man is installed in its place. Sharath directs it and later carries the title Paramaguru. The maxim printed on studio walls in a dozen countries is his in speech only: no letter, no book, and no transcript records him composing the sentence, and every student who heard him agrees that he said it.
stops.quote: Do your practice and all is coming.
stops.quote_source: An oral maxim of Jois recorded by his students, best anchored to Guy Donahaye and Eddie Stern, Guruji: A Portrait of Sri K. stops.name: New Delhi, the archive and the missing manuscript
stops.date_confidence: the claimed discovery is undated tradition; the date here marks the scholarly reckoning, not the alleged find
stops.campa: The Yoga Korunta is looked for where Krishnamacharya said he found it, in the National Archives of India, and is not there. Mark Singleton treats its existence as unverified; a Yoga Journal editor counts at least five mutually inconsistent versions of the discovery, one of which moves it to a palm leaf in Calcutta. Krishnamacharya cites it in neither Yoga Makaranda nor Yogasanagalu. Wikipedia files the article under hoaxes in India. Several hundred thousand people practice a sequence whose charter cannot be produced.
suggested_refs: The National Archives of India, Janpath, New Delhi, named as the manuscript's source in one of five versions
sources: Mark Singleton, Yoga Body (2010), as cited there

stops.name: Manhattan, the testimony published
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the years of publication; none of the three publications was fetched directly this session
stops.campa: Anneke Lucas publishes her account on YogaCityNYC in 2016. Yoga Journal runs a mea culpa on sexual assault in the Ashtanga community in 2018, and on the eighth of November 2019 the New York Times prints two pieces naming Karen Rain and Jubilee Cooke. Wikipedia states that Jois systematically sexually abused some of his female and male students, in Mysore and while traveling, until his death. He is seven years dead when the first account appears and answers none of it.
suggested_refs: Yoga Journal, 'Sexual Assault in the Ashtanga Yoga Community: A Mea Culpa' (2018); New York Times, 8 November 2019
sources: Reporting summarized in the verified research pool; the original articles were not reachable this session

stops.name: Mysore, the grandson's statement
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year; the original Instagram post was not opened this session
stops.campa: Sharath Jois posts a statement acknowledging the accounts. He does not dispute them and he does not leave the seat. The institute keeps teaching the sequence, under the founder's name on the sign, in the same rooms, to students who arrive having read what was published. The lineage has no procedure for this: its authority passes by blood and by hands laid on bodies, and what is alleged is about hands laid on bodies. He holds the seat five more years and dies in it.
stops.quote: It brings me immense pain that I also witnessed him giving improper adjustments
stops.quote_source: R. Sharath Jois, 2019 public statement, as quoted in Wikipedia, 'K. Pattabhi Jois'; the original post was not accessed

stops.name: Humpback Rocks, the successor dies
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the coordinate is Humpback Rocks on the Blue Ridge Parkway, Augusta County, not the unrelated South Georgia feature of the same name
stops.campa: On the eleventh of November 2024 Sharath Jois dies of a heart attack while hiking with students near Humpback Rocks on the Blue Ridge Parkway in Virginia, during a visit connected to the University of Virginia. He is fifty-three. Fifteen years after the founder, the man who held the lineage's central authority dies abroad, mid-tour, among students, on a mountain in the country his grandfather first reached at sixty. The seat empties in the middle of a teaching season.
suggested_refs: Humpback Rocks, Milepost 5.8, Blue Ridge Parkway, Augusta County, Virginia

stops.name: Mysore, the lineage divided
stops.date_confidence: ongoing since 2009; the date is a marker for a continuing state of affairs rather than an event
stops.campa: Saraswathi Rangaswamy, the founder's daughter, and her own daughter Sharmila run a separate school in the city; Manju Jois has taught in the United States for decades. The authority that ran through one house in Lakshmipuram now runs through several addresses in one city and several thousand rooms outside it. The atlas keeps him in its body-culture wing beside Joseph Pilates, another man who built a system out of his century's appetite for disciplined bodies and left it to be taught by people who never met him.
suggested_refs: Saraswathi Rangaswamy and Sharmila Mahesh's school in Mysore; joseph_pilates.journey.json, body-culture wing
